entries.clue: Show the way, swilling ale, fellow! (4,2)

indicatorNotes.swilling: Ale being swilled is sloshed around, so its letters are stirred.

blocks.note: a don is a college fellow

annotation.surface: Someone taking charge of a pub crowd while a drinking mate knocks back his pint.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma and exclamation make 'fellow' look like a form of address; it is a university don.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain phrasal-verb synonym: leading on means going ahead so others follow.

entries.clue: Learn less than you should as an actor in waiting? (10)

blocks.note: under = short of the proper amount

annotation.surface: A lazy actor who doesn't learn his lines properly.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word itself reads as 'under-study', exactly what a slacking understudy does.
annotation.definitionFit: An understudy waits in the wings, ready to take over a role if the lead actor cannot go on.

entries.clue: Washington heard about missile tip (7)

indicatorNotes.about: Letters that are about are turned around and moved, so HEARD is rearranged.

blocks.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

annotation.surface: The US government has been told of a missile.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Washington' as the US government is the misdirection; here it is the state's two-letter code.
annotation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive front end of a missile.

entries.clue: see26ac.
In the sack, free end of leg and cut (8)

indicatorNotes.end of: The end of a word is its final letter.

blocks.note: abed = in bed; the sack is slang for bed

annotation.surface: Someone in bed freeing the end of an injured leg, then trimming something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the sack' does double duty: it is the outer word and also says where the rest goes. 'Free' reads as an adjective in the surface, but here it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book or speech shortened by trimming passages has been cut in exactly this sense.

entries.clue: Band, Mangled Testes – vote to replace son (6)

indicatorNotes.Mangled: Something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the letters of TESTES are scrambled.
indicatorNotes.to replace: One letter goes in where another comes out.

blocks.note: you mark an X on a ballot paper to vote
s = son, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A rock group with a gruesomely named line-up, put to a vote.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap one S of TESTES for X to get TEXTES, then scramble. 'Band, Mangled Testes' reads like a band name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by kind: a group of six performers is one sort of band.

entries.clue: Fresh large NDA settlement, that's what Trump wants! (9)

indicatorNotes.settlement: A settlement rearranges things into a new order, so the letters of NDA are resettled.

blocks.note: green = fresh, as in green vegetables
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A new hush-money deal with a non-disclosure agreement, just the sort of thing Trump is after.
annotation.walkthrough: An NDA is a non-disclosure agreement, which makes 'settlement' read as a legal payout; here it only resettles three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Donald Trump has repeatedly said the US should acquire Greenland.

entries.clue: Opponent of David's record turned up with a hit broadcast (7)

indicatorNotes.turned up: In a down answer, turning a word up makes it read bottom to top.
indicatorNotes.broadcast: Seed that is broadcast is scattered, so the letters of A HIT are spread about.

annotation.surface: A rival of some musician named David whose record went to the top as a broadcast hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'hit' paint the music charts; the David is the biblical shepherd boy.
annotation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant David fought and killed with a sling.

entries.clue: Maybe Rayner's task is to hide former record (6)

indicatorNotes.is to hide: What hides another thing holds it out of sight inside itself.

blocks.note: an EP, extended play, is an old record format

annotation.surface: A politician's job is to bury something from her past.
annotation.walkthrough: Angela Rayner was the UK's Deputy Prime Minister; 'maybe' flags her as one example. The ''s' is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Rayner served as deputy to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, so she is an example of a deputy.

entries.clue: Earl's knob lengthened somewhat? (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: Somewhat means a part of, so the answer is part of the words that follow.

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: A cheeky remark about an aristocrat's anatomy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knob' is British slang for penis, which is the ribald surface; it only carries the first letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An earl is one rank of the peerage, so the definition is by example of the class.

entries.clue: Say party on left rejected retreat (5)

indicatorNotes.rejected: What is rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards.

blocks.note: L = left; DO sits on it

annotation.surface: A political party's left wing turned down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party on left' sounds like politics; it is just a do and an L. Build EGDOL, then read it backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house used as a retreat, such as a hunting lodge.

entries.clue: Who'll put you under Tony – shit, lost without power! (9)

indicatorNotes.lost: Letters that are lost have lost their way, so TONY SHIT is scrambled.
indicatorNotes.without: Without means outside: the scrambled letters go round the P.

annotation.surface: Someone cursing a man called Tony who has lost his power.
annotation.walkthrough: Put P after HY in the scrambled letters. 'Put you under' sounds like a threat or anaesthetic; it is hypnosis.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Put under' is the idiom for inducing a trance, the stage performer's trade.

entries.clue: Not a complaint expected of a retainer? (7)

annotation.definition: Not a complaint expected of a retainer?
annotation.surface: A loyal old servant who never grumbles.
annotation.walkthrough: A retainer reads as a family servant; the other sense is something that retains, a memory that holds on to things, and that is the last thing to lose its memory.
annotation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a complaint in the sense of an ailment.

blocks.note: the surface hears a grumble; the setter means an illness, a medical complaint
reads as a faithful family servant; the setter means something that retains, like a good memory, the last thing to forget

entries.clue: Considered: "However, Trump just got started" (7)

indicatorNotes.just got started: What has just got started has only its first letter so far.

annotation.surface: A pundit weighing in: Trump has only just begun.
annotation.definitionFit: Considered, as in 'she considered it', means thought about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trump' reads as the man again, as in 7 across; only his first letter is used, and 'just got started' says so.

entries.clue: Madonna's mad with Ben – "not one to share responsibilities" (3-3,4)

indicatorNotes.mad: Mad letters are out of their right order.

annotation.surface: A pop star furious with a partner called Ben who won't pull his weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The ''s' is 'is': Madonna is mad, that is, scrambled, along with Ben.
annotation.definitionFit: A one-man band does every job himself rather than sharing the work.

entries.clue: Bollocks stink – infection (6)

blocks.note: hum = a bad smell, British slang

annotation.surface: A crude complaint about a smelly infection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bollocks' is British slang for nonsense as well as testicles; with 'infection' after it, the anatomy reading wins at first.
annotation.definitionFit: Humbug and bollocks both mean nonsense.

entries.clue: Sexist quality of vibrating gismo covering tops of your natty Y-fronts (8)

indicatorNotes.vibrating: Vibrating shakes things, so the letters of GISMO move about.
indicatorNotes.covering: In a down answer, what covers sits above.
indicatorNotes.tops of: The top of each word is its first letter.

annotation.surface: A sex toy advertised with smart men's underpants, which is sexist.
annotation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are British men's briefs. The surface is so risqué that the definition hides in plain sight at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Misogyny, hatred of or prejudice against women, is the quality of being sexist.

entries.clue: Mock Dirty Den covered in drink (4,2)

indicatorNotes.Dirty: Dirty letters are messed up, so DEN is rearranged.
indicatorNotes.covered in: What is covered in something has it all around it.

annotation.surface: Dirty Den, the EastEnders pub landlord, getting drenched in a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Dirty Den was a villainous landlord in the BBC soap EastEnders, so the name hides an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a parody or satire mocks its target.

entries.clue: Fleshy thing turning up with politician relatives (7)

indicatorNotes.turning: Turning a word round makes it read backwards.

annotation.surface: A politician turning up with his relatives in tow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like arriving; 'up' is the word turned. 'Fleshy thing' is fair: a pumpkin is a fleshy fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is a large fruit with thick flesh.

entries.clue: Iron Lady atop George Galloway? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes a location, standing for the thing found there: what sits on George Galloway's head.

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

annotation.surface: Margaret Thatcher towering over a left-wing politician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' is Margaret Thatcher's nickname, but it splits into Fe and a name. George Galloway, the British left-wing politician, is known for his fedora hat.
annotation.definitionFit: A fedora is the soft brimmed hat George Galloway habitually wears.

entries.clue: In need, if I celebrated erection (7)

indicatorNotes.In: The answer is in the words that follow.

blocks.note: the letters start at the end of the first word and run through the middle two into the start of the last

annotation.surface: A cheeky boast about celebrating an erection when it's needed.
annotation.walkthrough: The innuendo does the hiding: 'erection' also means something built.
annotation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large building, something erected.

entries.clue: To wrongly finger some character is empty, desperate (7)

indicatorNotes.desperate: Desperate letters are thrown into disorder.

annotation.surface: Framing someone for a crime when you've no evidence and are desperate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finger some character' reads as accusing a person; it is pressing the wrong key for a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To mistype is to hit the wrong key when typing a character.

entries.clue: Handy device that's big in Alabama (6)

blocks.note: a handy device is a portable phone; Handy is also what Germans call one
a big place in Alabama, the port city on the Gulf coast

annotation.surface: A useful gadget that's popular in the American South.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big in Alabama' reads as popular there; it means a big place in the state, the port city of Mobile.
annotation.definitionFit: A mobile phone is a handy device, and Mobile is one of Alabama's largest cities.

entries.clue: Indian city in stupid plan (7)

indicatorNotes.in: The city goes inside the next word.

blocks.note: Agra, home of the Taj Mahal

annotation.surface: A foolish scheme for an Indian city.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drawing that lays out how parts fit is a plan.
annotation.walkthrough: Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal; tuck it inside DIM.

entries.clue: Rush to have sex? Correct again! (2-4)

blocks.note: a rush is a reed-like water plant

annotation.surface: Someone in a hurry to get into bed, told they've got it right again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush' reads as hurry; it is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix re- supplies 'again', and editing a text is correcting it.

entries.clue: Quit one who taps Dicky (6,3)

blocks.note: a bugger plants listening devices to tap phones
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, like off

annotation.surface: Leave a man called Dicky who keeps touching people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quit' is the imperative: bugger off is British slang for go away.
annotation.definitionFit: Quit, as an order, means leave, which is what 'bugger off' rudely tells someone to do.

entries.clue: Parrot house downsized after energy cuts introduced (4)

indicatorNotes.introduced: What is introduced shows only its first letter.
indicatorNotes.downsized: A downsized word has lost some of its size.
indicatorNotes.after: The house comes after the other letters.

blocks.note: HOUSE cut to HO, its usual abbreviation

annotation.surface: A pet bird's home shrinking once energy cuts arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is the verb, to repeat. 'Energy cuts' reads as one phrase, but energy and cuts give a letter each.
annotation.definitionFit: To parrot and to echo both mean to repeat what someone else says.

entries.clue: (& 4dn) Be a burglar or beatnik bum (5)

indicatorNotes.bum: Bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are faulty in order.

annotation.surface: A choice between a life of crime or dropping out as a beatnik layabout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link word, but it is fodder; 'bum' reads as a tramp, but is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Burglary is forcing entry into a building, so the phrasal verb describes the burglar's act.

entries.clue: One leaves to throw up a meal (5)

indicatorNotes.leaves: When one leaves, its letter goes.

blocks.note: to launch is to throw up into the air

annotation.surface: Someone who has to leave the table to vomit their dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as vomit, apt with a meal; it is launching something skyward.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the midday meal is one of the day's meals.

entries.clue: In case son screwed up, going up in life (9)

indicatorNotes.screwed up: Something screwed up is crumpled and muddled.

annotation.surface: A parent hedging against a son who might make a mess of his career.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' as an anagram indicator sits next to 'going up', making 'up' look like part of the definition's direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for rising, with 'in life' adding the sense of climbing socially or in rank.
